title: Over 5.63 Lakh Villages Covered with Liquid Waste Management Arrangements under SBM(G) Phase II
subtitle: SBM(G) Phase II Focuses on Sustainable Sanitation and Greywater Management in Villages
body_text:
Sanitation is a State subject. Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)] Phase II is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by States/UTs in respective jurisdictions. SBM(G) Phase II was launched with effect from 1 st April 2020, with the focus on ODF sustainability with Solid & Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) and visual cleanliness in villages i.e. to convert villages from ODF to ODF Plus (Model). Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) monitors the status of Grey Water Management (GWM) under SBM(G) Phase-II as reported by States/UTs on the SBM(G) Integrated Management Information System (IMIS).
As per the information reported by the States/UTs on the SBM(G) IMIS, as on 07.08.2026, out of 5,86,944 villages 5,63,809 villages are reported to have been covered with Liquid Waste Management arrangements.
As per the SBM(G) Phase-II guidelines, various interventions can be undertaken for GWM such as constructions of soak-pit, leach-pit, magic-pit or kitchen garden at household level and Waste Stabilization Ponds, Constructed Wetland, Decentralized Wastewater Treatment System (DEWATS) and Phytorid Technology at community/village level. The SBM(G) IMIS does not capture details of category-wise rural drains (for example: open, closed, kutcha, or pucca drain) or unconnected or inadequate open drains.
As per the data reported by States/UTs on SBM(G) IMIS, as on 07.08.2026, a total of 42,98,194 community GWM assets have been reported. The State/UT-wise details of community GWM assets created, including community soak pits, drainage facilities and community treatment systems, as per data reported by the States/UTs on SBM(G) IMIS may be seen at Annexure-I .
DDWS, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India has been providing financial and technical support to the States/UTs for implementation of SBM(G) Phase-II. In each Financial Year, funds are allocated to States/UTs based on their approved Annual Implementation Plan (AIP), past performance and budget availability.
States/UTs can plan for providing sanitation and SLWM facilities under the program as per demand, local preferences, etc. as per their AIP. Apart from budgetary support from DDWS and the corresponding State share, the remaining funds are to be dovetailed by States/UTs from the Finance Commission grants to Rural Local Bodies and MGNREGS/VB-G RAM G. States/UTs can also converge funds from other Central/State schemes, as applicable, CSR funds, MPLADS/MLALADS and revenue generation though business models, etc.
In addition to the SBM(G) Phase II Operational Guidelines, technical manuals and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are provided by DDWS to States/UTs for capacity building of Gram Panchayats on various components of the programme. Under SBM(G) Phase II, for Greywater Management, financial support of up to Rs.280 per capita for villages up to 5000 population and up to Rs.660 per capita for villages above 5000 population is provided. In addition, awareness generation and capacity building interventions are be conducted by States/UTs at various levels to promote community participation, behavioural change and capacity building regarding GWM, including for preventing stagnation of wastewater in rural areas.

enrichment.summary: As of 7 August 2026, 5,63,809 out of 5,86,944 villages (about 96%) have been covered with Liquid Waste Management arrangements under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II, as reported by States/UTs on the SBM(G) IMIS. A total of 42,98,194 community Grey Water Management (GWM) assets have been created nationwide, including soak pits, drainage facilities and treatment systems. This information was shared by Minister of State for Jal Shakti V. Somanna in a written reply in Lok Sabha.
enrichment.context:
SBM(G) Phase II, launched from 1 April 2020, moves beyond the Open Defecation Free (ODF) achievement of Phase I towards ODF Plus status, emphasizing Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) and visual cleanliness in villages. Since sanitation is a State subject under the Constitution, the scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by States/UTs with technical and financial support from the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. Greywater (used household water from kitchens, bathing, washing) management is a critical rural sanitation challenge since, unlike black water/sewage, it is often left unmanaged, causing stagnation, breeding grounds for vectors, and health hazards.

Under the scheme, interventions range from household-level soak pits/leach pits/magic pits to community-level solutions like Waste Stabilization Ponds, Constructed Wetlands, DEWATS, and Phytorid technology. Financing is need-based: DDWS provides up to Rs.280 per capita for smaller villages (population up to 5000) and Rs.660 per capita for larger villages, supplemented by State shares, 15th Finance Commission grants to rural local bodies, MGNREGS/VB-GRAM G funds, CSR, MPLADS/MLALADS, and revenue models. This reflects a broader shift in India's sanitation policy from a toilet-construction-centric approach (Phase I) to holistic environmental sanitation and sustainability, aligning with SDG 6 (clean water and sanitation) and India's rural development goals.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II:
1. It focuses on converting villages from ODF to ODF Plus status through Solid and Liquid Waste Management.
2. Sanitation is a Union subject under the Constitution of India, hence SBM(G) is centrally implemented.
3. Financial support for Greywater Management under the scheme is uniform regardless of village population size.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. Sanitation is a State subject (not Union), and SBM(G) Phase II is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by States/UTs. Financial support for GWM varies by village population (up to Rs.280 per capita for villages up to 5000 population and up to Rs.660 per capita for larger villages), so it is not uniform.

prelims_questions.question:
Which of the following technologies/structures are used for Greywater Management under SBM(G) Phase II?
1. Soak pits
2. Constructed Wetlands
3. DEWATS (Decentralized Wastewater Treatment System)
4. Phytorid Technology
Select the correct answer using the code below:
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, all four—soak pits (household level), and Constructed Wetlands, DEWATS, and Phytorid Technology (community/village level)—are interventions permitted under SBM(G) Phase II for Greywater Management.
